skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

15.     mem::{

17.         paging::TableEntry,
18.     },
19.     x86::mem::paging::{
20.         flags::{
21.             AccessedFlag,
22.             CopyOnWriteFlag,

24.             PageCacheDisableFlag,

36. // Page Table Entry Flags
37. //==================================================================================================
38. 
39. ///
40. /// # Description
41. ///
42. /// A type that represents flags of a page table entry.
43. ///
44. #[verus_verify]
45. #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
46. pub struct PageTableEntryFlags {
47.     /// Present flag.
48.     present: PresentFlag,
49.     /// Read/write flag.
50.     read_write: ReadWriteFlag,
51.     /// User/supervisor flag.
52.     user_supervisor: UserSupervisorFlag,
53.     /// Page write-through flag.
54.     page_write_through: PageWriteThroughFlag,
55.     /// Page cache disable flag.
56.     page_cache_disable: PageCacheDisableFlag,
57.     /// Accessed flag.
58.     accessed: AccessedFlag,
59.     /// Dirty flag.
60.     dirty: DirtyFlag,
61.     /// Copy-on-write flag (OS-defined, stored in an AVL bit).
62.     cow: CopyOnWriteFlag,
63. }
64. 
65. impl PageTableEntryFlags {
66.     ///
67.     /// # Description
68.     ///
69.     /// Constructs a [`PageTableEntryFlags`] with the given flags.
70.     ///
71.     /// # Parameters
72.     ///
73.     /// - `present`: The present flag.
74.     /// - `read_write`: The read/write flag.
75.     /// - `user_supervisor`: The user/supervisor flag.
76.     /// - `page_write_through`: The page write-through flag.
77.     /// - `page_cache_disable`: The page cache disable flag.
78.     /// - `accessed`: The accessed flag.
79.     /// - `dirty`: The dirty flag.
80.     ///
81.     /// # Returns
82.     ///
83.     /// A new [`PageTableEntryFlags`] with the given flags.
84.     ///
85.     #[cfg_attr(verus_keep_ghost, allow(unused, verus_impl_method_marker))]
86.     #[verus_spec(result =>
87.         ensures
88.             result@ == spec_pte_flags_new(
89.                 present,
90.                 read_write,
91.                 user_supervisor,
92.                 page_write_through,
93.                 page_cache_disable,
94.                 accessed,
95.                 dirty,
96.             ),
97.     )]
98.     pub fn new(
99.         present: PresentFlag,
100.         read_write: ReadWriteFlag,
101.         user_supervisor: UserSupervisorFlag,
102.         page_write_through: PageWriteThroughFlag,
103.         page_cache_disable: PageCacheDisableFlag,
104.         accessed: AccessedFlag,
105.         dirty: DirtyFlag,
106.     ) -> Self {
107.         Self {
108.             present,
109.             read_write,
110.             user_supervisor,
111.             page_write_through,
112.             page_cache_disable,
113.             accessed,
114.             dirty,
115.             cow: CopyOnWriteFlag::NotCopyOnWrite,
116.         }
117.     }
118. 
119.     ///
120.     /// # Description
121.     ///
122.     /// Constructs a [`PageTableEntryFlags`] from a raw value.
123.     ///
124.     /// # Parameters
125.     ///
126.     /// - `value`: The raw value.
127.     ///
128.     /// # Returns
129.     ///
130.     /// A [`PageTableEntryFlags`].
131.     ///
132.     fn from_raw_value(value: PteWord) -> Self {
133.         Self {
134.             present: PresentFlag::from_raw_value(value),
135.             read_write: ReadWriteFlag::from_raw_value(value),
136.             user_supervisor: UserSupervisorFlag::from_raw_value(value),
137.             page_write_through: PageWriteThroughFlag::from_raw_value(value),
138.             page_cache_disable: PageCacheDisableFlag::from_raw_value(value),
139.             accessed: AccessedFlag::from_raw_value(value),
140.             dirty: DirtyFlag::from_raw_value(value),
141.             cow: CopyOnWriteFlag::from_raw_value(value),
142.         }
143.     }
144. 
145.     ///
146.     /// # Description
147.     ///
148.     /// Converts a [`PageTableEntryFlags`] into a raw value.
149.     ///
150.     /// # Returns
151.     ///
152.     /// The raw value.
153.     ///
154.     fn into_raw_value(self) -> PteWord {
155.         let mut value: PteWord = 0;
156. 
157.         value |= self.present.into_raw_value();
158.         value |= self.read_write.into_raw_value();
159.         value |= self.user_supervisor.into_raw_value();
160.         value |= self.page_write_through.into_raw_value();
161.         value |= self.page_cache_disable.into_raw_value();
162.         value |= self.accessed.into_raw_value();
163.         value |= self.dirty.into_raw_value();
164.         value |= self.cow.into_raw_value();
165. 
166.         value
167.     }
168. 
169.     ///
170.     /// # Description
171.     ///
172.     /// Checks if the present flag is set.
173.     ///
174.     /// # Returns
175.     ///
176.     /// `true` if the present flag is set, `false` otherwise.
177.     ///
178.     #[inline(always)]
179.     #[verus_spec(result =>
180.         ensures result == self@.present,
181.     )]
182.     pub fn is_present(&self) -> bool {
183.         matches!(self.present, PresentFlag::Present)
184.     }
185. 
186.     ///
187.     /// # Description
188.     ///
189.     /// Checks if the user flag is set (i.e., user-mode access is allowed).
190.     ///
191.     /// # Returns
192.     ///
193.     /// `true` if the user flag is set, `false` otherwise.
194.     ///
195.     #[inline(always)]
196.     pub fn is_user(&self) -> bool {
197.         matches!(self.user_supervisor, UserSupervisorFlag::User)
198.     }
199. 
200.     ///
201.     /// # Description
202.     ///
203.     /// Checks if the read/write flag is set (i.e., the page is writable).
204.     ///
205.     /// # Returns
206.     ///
207.     /// `true` if the page is writable, `false` otherwise.
208.     ///
209.     #[inline(always)]
210.     pub fn is_writable(&self) -> bool {
211.         matches!(self.read_write, ReadWriteFlag::ReadWrite)
212.     }
213. 
214.     ///
215.     /// # Description
216.     ///
217.     /// Sets read/write flag.
218.     ///
219.     /// # Parameters
220.     ///
221.     /// - `read_write`: The read/write flag.
222.     ///
223.     #[inline(always)]
224.     pub fn set_read_write(&mut self, read_write: ReadWriteFlag) {
225.         self.read_write = read_write;
226.     }
227. 
228.     ///
229.     /// # Description
230.     ///
231.     /// Sets user/supervisor flag.
232.     ///
233.     /// # Parameters
234.     ///
235.     /// - `user_supervisor`: The user/supervisor flag.
236.     ///
237.     #[inline(always)]
238.     pub fn set_user_supervisor(&mut self, user_supervisor: UserSupervisorFlag) {
239.         self.user_supervisor = user_supervisor;
240.     }
241. 
242.     ///
243.     /// # Description
244.     ///
245.     /// Checks if the copy-on-write flag is set.
246.     ///
247.     /// # Returns
248.     ///
249.     /// `true` if the copy-on-write flag is set, `false` otherwise.
250.     ///
251.     #[inline(always)]
252.     pub fn is_cow(&self) -> bool {
253.         matches!(self.cow, CopyOnWriteFlag::CopyOnWrite)
254.     }
255. 
256.     ///
257.     /// # Description
258.     ///
259.     /// Sets the copy-on-write flag.
260.     ///
261.     /// # Parameters
262.     ///
263.     /// - `cow`: The copy-on-write flag.
264.     ///
265.     #[inline(always)]
266.     pub fn set_cow(&mut self, cow: CopyOnWriteFlag) {
267.         self.cow = cow;
268.     }
269. }

276. /// # Description
277. ///
278. /// A type that represents a page table entry.
279. ///
280. #[verus_verify]
281. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
282. pub struct PageTableEntry {
283.     /// Flags.
284.     flags: PageTableEntryFlags,
285.     /// Physical address of the page frame.
286.     frame: FrameNumber,
287. }
288. 
289. impl PageTableEntry {
290.     /// Size in bytes of the hardware page table entry representation.
291.     pub const SIZE: usize = ::core::mem::size_of::<PteWord>();
292. 
293.     ///
294.     /// # Description
295.     ///
296.     /// Constructs a [`PageTableEntry`] with the given flags and frame.
297.     ///
298.     /// # Parameters
299.     ///
300.     /// - `flags`: The flags.
301.     /// - `frame`: The frame number.
302.     ///
303.     /// # Returns
304.     ///
305.     /// A [`PageTableEntry`].
306.     ///
307.     #[cfg_attr(verus_keep_ghost, allow(unused, verus_impl_method_marker))]
308.     #[verus_spec(result =>
309.         ensures
310.             result@ == spec_pte_new(flags@, frame@),
311.             result.inv(),
312.     )]
313.     pub fn new(flags: PageTableEntryFlags, frame: FrameNumber) -> Self {
314.         proof! { use_type_invariant(frame); }
315.         Self { flags, frame }
316.     }

319.     /// # Description
320.     ///
321.     /// Constructs a [`PageTableEntry`] from a raw value.
322.     ///
323.     /// # Parameters
324.     ///
325.     /// - `value`: The raw value.
326.     ///
327.     /// # Returns
328.     ///
329.     /// - `Some(`[`PageTableEntry`]`)`: If the raw value is valid.
330.     /// - `None`: Otherwise.
331.     ///
332.     pub fn from_raw_value(value: PteWord) -> Option<Self> {
333.         Some(Self {
334.             flags: PageTableEntryFlags::from_raw_value(value),
335.             frame: FrameNumber::from_raw_value(value as usize >> mem::FRAME_SHIFT)?,

349.         let mut value: PteWord = 0;
350. 
351.         value |= self.flags.into_raw_value();
352.         value |= (self.frame.into_raw_value() << crate::mem::FRAME_SHIFT) as PteWord;
353. 
354.         value
355.     }

20. // The copy-on-write projection is PTE-specific (the PDE sibling has a page-size bit instead), so it

27. // PageTableEntryFlags — abstract value (the eight control bits)
28. //==================================================================================================
29. 
30. // To a caller a flags bundle is exactly its eight paging-control bits. The bit-packing into the
31. // raw `PteWord` is hidden (the View is `closed`), realizing the encoding-independence the caller
32. // analysis demands. The single structural difference from the `pde` sibling is the OS-defined
33. // `cow` (copy-on-write, AVL) bit in place of the PDE's hardware `large_page` (PS) bit.
34. pub struct PteFlagsView {
35.     /// Present (P) bit — the entry maps a page (`is_present`).
36.     pub present: bool,
37.     /// Read/Write (R/W) bit — writes permitted (`is_writable`).
38.     pub writable: bool,
39.     /// User/Supervisor (U/S) bit — user-mode access permitted (`is_user`).
40.     pub user: bool,
41.     /// Page-Write-Through (PWT) bit.
42.     pub write_through: bool,
43.     /// Page-Cache-Disable (PCD) bit.
44.     pub cache_disabled: bool,
45.     /// Accessed (A) bit.
46.     pub accessed: bool,
47.     /// Dirty (D) bit.
48.     pub dirty: bool,
49.     /// Copy-on-write (OS-defined AVL) bit — set by `set_cow`, read by `is_cow`.
50.     pub cow: bool,
51. }

53. impl View for PageTableEntryFlags {
54.     type V = PteFlagsView;
55. 
56.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> PteFlagsView {
57.         PteFlagsView {
58.             present: spec_present_set(self.present),
59.             writable: spec_rw_set(self.read_write),
60.             user: spec_us_set(self.user_supervisor),
61.             write_through: spec_pwt_set(self.page_write_through),
62.             cache_disabled: spec_pcd_set(self.page_cache_disable),
63.             accessed: spec_a_set(self.accessed),
64.             dirty: spec_d_set(self.dirty),

103. // PageTableEntry — abstract value (flags + frame)
104. //==================================================================================================
105. 
106. // A PTE is the pair `(flags, frame)`. The frame is abstracted as its integer index (the
107. // `FrameNumber` View); the physical base address it yields is *derived* (`frame * FRAME_SIZE`),
108. // never stored.
109. pub struct PteView {
110.     /// The eight control bits this entry was built with.
111.     pub flags: PteFlagsView,
112.     /// The frame index this entry points at (== the inner `FrameNumber`'s `@`).
113.     pub frame: int,
114. }

116. impl View for PageTableEntry {
117.     type V = PteView;
118. 
119.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> PteView {
120.         PteView { flags: self.flags@, frame: self.frame@ }
121.     }
122. }

124. impl PageTableEntry {
125.     // The only real constraint is the frame bound, inherited verbatim from the `FrameNumber` type
126.     // invariant. It is what makes the (out-of-scope) `frame_address` total and overflow-free: the
127.     // derived physical base `frame * FRAME_SIZE` is well-defined and cannot overflow `usize`. (The
128.     // flags carry no cross-field constraint — `PageTableEntryFlags::inv` is vacuously `true` — so
129.     // they add nothing here.)
130.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
131.         0 <= self@.frame <= FrameNumber::spec_max()
132.     }
133. }

138.     PteView { flags, frame }
